description: Named aesthetic archetypes keyed by material type. The planner picks ONE archetype per run; prompt assembly injects that archetype's compositional grammar into the execution_prompt so the model has concrete handholds instead of generic mood words. Each archetype declares: reference_work (who/where the aesthetic lives), compositional_grammar (one sentence describing layout/framing), color_rule (one sentence on palette discipline), rendering_finish (one sentence on surface treatment), signature_moves (2-3 concrete do's), and example_bans (2-3 concrete don'ts). Rotation across a material's archetype set prevents every run from defaulting to the same paradigm.

concept-illustration.name: Penguin Classics paperback cover
concept-illustration.reference_work: Penguin Classics editions by Coralie Bickford-Smith and earlier series
concept-illustration.compositional_grammar: One symbolic motif occupying the center-upper third, framed by generous negative space with a subtle decorative border or geometric frame; typography (if any) treated as integral layout, not overlay.
concept-illustration.color_rule: Two-to-three ink colors from the brand palette on a warm paper-toned ground; one saturated accent against muted field.
concept-illustration.rendering_finish: Flat woodcut or linocut quality — visible carving texture, no gradients, no 3D shading, no photographic grain.
signature_moves: central symbolic motif as the whole composition, not an icon-plus-text lockup
1-2mm decorative inner border with subtle pattern repeat
hand-set typographic feel when any text is present
example_bans: glossy 3D renders or realistic photographic shading
multiple icons arranged in a grid

concept-illustration.name: Charley Harper minimal realism
concept-illustration.reference_work: Charley Harper's mid-century nature illustrations and Ford Times plates
concept-illustration.compositional_grammar: Subject reduced to geometric primitives (circle, rectangle, triangle) and placed with intentional asymmetry; silhouette over detail; the natural form reads clearly but is never rendered with anatomical fidelity.
concept-illustration.color_rule: 4-6 flat colors total, carefully selected for contrast and rhythm; no gradients; black ink used sparingly for defining edges.
concept-illustration.rendering_finish: Pure flat vector with hand-drawn line quality; visible but intentional imperfection; silk-screen feel rather than digital-sharp.
signature_moves: one subject, geometrically abstracted, positioned off-center
negative space as equal compositional partner, not leftover
limited palette that reads bold but never neon

concept-illustration.name: Kyoto garden stillness (sumi-e)
concept-illustration.reference_work: Japanese sumi-e ink-wash paintings and Ryoan-ji rock-garden compositions
concept-illustration.compositional_grammar: Radical asymmetry anchored in Ma (間) negative space; one focal gesture placed against roughly 70% emptiness; the composition feels paused rather than staged.
concept-illustration.color_rule: Monochrome or near-monochrome — ink on paper — plus at most one muted accent from the brand palette.
concept-illustration.rendering_finish: Ink-wash bleed edges, visible brushstroke texture, paper grain underneath, no hard geometric edges.
signature_moves: enormous negative space; the subject is small in frame
brushstroke energy and wetness visible in the mark
contemplative rhythm — calm, not empty

concept-illustration.name: Criterion Collection title card
concept-illustration.reference_work: Criterion Collection box art and opening title cards
concept-illustration.compositional_grammar: Title-card framing: typographic block + single resonant image, letterboxed with generous negative borders; the image carries the film's whole argument; typography is calm, authoritative, and visually integrated.
concept-illustration.color_rule: Restrained palette of 2-4 colors; image warmth + one bold type-hue (often cream, bone, or oxblood); no saturation above 70%.
concept-illustration.rendering_finish: Film-still clarity without photographic glare; painterly if illustration, archival-photograph-soft if photo-derived.
signature_moves: letterbox bands as intentional composition frame
one dominant image anchors the meaning, not a collage
typography sits at the edge in a serif or geometric-sans with measured confidence

concept-illustration.name: Noma foraging journal plate
concept-illustration.reference_work: René Redzepi's Noma foraging journals, field-guide botanical plates
concept-illustration.compositional_grammar: Specimen-on-paper: a single organic subject floats centered on an off-white field with hand-noted annotation space around it; the composition feels excerpted from a larger journal rather than designed-for-display.
concept-illustration.color_rule: Muted natural palette — sage, ochre, charcoal, bone — plus one ember accent; never synthetic-vivid.
concept-illustration.rendering_finish: Botanical-illustration precision with hand-inked edges and watercolor wash fills; paper grain visible; archival feel.
signature_moves: one specimen, centered, isolated
hand-noted annotation or dated marginalia as texture
soft watercolor wash for fills, never flat CMYK

brand-scene.name: Japanese kogei (craft) workshop practice
brand-scene.reference_work: Japanese kogei workshops documented in Monocle and Kinfolk
brand-scene.compositional_grammar: Quiet workshop interior mid-practice: hands at work on a craft surface, daylight raking in from one side, tools arranged as evidence of process rather than styled; the room feels inhabited, not staged.
brand-scene.color_rule: Wood tones + raw material (clay, textile, paper) + the brand palette as lighting tint; all neutrals are warm, no cold grays.
brand-scene.rendering_finish: Documentary-photograph quality — soft natural grain, no high-key retouching, dust and imperfection visible.
signature_moves: hands mid-action, tools in use or at rest from recent use
raking daylight from a single window or skylight
material textures (wood grain, clay, paper fiber) read clearly
example_bans: empty architectural mood with no activity

brand-scene.name: Aesop apothecary shelf
brand-scene.reference_work: Aesop retail interiors by Snøhetta, Studio Ko, March Studio
brand-scene.compositional_grammar: Horizontal shelving as the governing grid; products arranged as a calm typology; one focal action (pick, pour, arrange) anchors the frame; the room's material language carries more weight than any single object.
brand-scene.color_rule: Warm neutral with one amber-glass accent and the brand's darker tone as a shadow base; no cold whites, no synthetic blacks.
brand-scene.rendering_finish: Softly-lit retail photography feel — diffused daylight, honest shadow, no product-catalog glare.
signature_moves: horizontal shelf grid as primary structure
single product or gesture as focal, surrounded by repetition
material honesty — visible wood grain, stone veining, paper texture
example_bans: studio-lit product shots with hard falloff
stock photography of generic retail interiors

brand-scene.name: Donald Judd Marfa studio
brand-scene.reference_work: Chinati Foundation installations and Donald Judd's Marfa working spaces
brand-scene.compositional_grammar: Empty industrial volume with one deliberate gesture: a single work surface, stacked boxes, or assembly mid-arrangement; the room reads as serious practice rather than styled space; the scale feels big and the activity feels small.
brand-scene.color_rule: Concrete, raw steel, desert daylight — the brand palette enters only through one applied surface (a panel, a chair, a fabric).
brand-scene.rendering_finish: Architectural-photography clarity — deep focus, natural shadow, no fill flash.
signature_moves: big empty volume, one small gesture inside it
industrial materials honest and unfinished
desert daylight or north-facing cool daylight
example_bans: cluttered shelving or multiple competing focal points
decorative objects with no evidence of use

brand-scene.name: Hermès orange atelier
brand-scene.reference_work: Hermès leather ateliers and Lanvin studio photography
brand-scene.compositional_grammar: Craftsperson mid-task at a well-worn wooden bench, tools laid out with practiced rhythm, single piece in-progress as focal element; the craft discipline carries the composition.
brand-scene.color_rule: Aged wood + leather tones + one bright atelier light tint; the brand palette enters through thread, fabric, or a signature accent color.
brand-scene.rendering_finish: Magazine-quality craft documentation — warm raking light, shallow depth of field on the hands and piece, background honest and out-of-focus.
signature_moves: hands and tools together in frame, mid-action
the in-progress piece is the hero, not a finished object
warm worn-wood palette as ground truth
example_bans: any pose of hands without an active task

landing-hero.name: Stripe spatial-gradient hero
landing-hero.reference_work: stripe.com hero treatments and Stripe Press covers
landing-hero.compositional_grammar: Split composition: left column copy, right column spatial-gradient art; the gradient reads as product architecture rendered in color space, not decoration; headline sits at the optical top of the copy column.
landing-hero.color_rule: Deep brand base with 1-2 accent hues in the gradient; the gradient's color choices should feel purposeful (map to product metaphor), not decorative.
landing-hero.rendering_finish: Crisp digital; rendered in 3D or vector but feels dimensional; clean edge treatment, no noise overlay, subtle.
signature_moves: left-copy / right-gradient composition
spatial-gradient shape implies product architecture
monospace or tight-grotesk headline voice
example_bans: centered-headline over generic dark hero image

landing-hero.name: Linear motion-diagram hero
landing-hero.reference_work: linear.app hero treatments and Arc browser announcements
landing-hero.compositional_grammar: Full-bleed dark-mode surface with an illuminated node-edge diagram as the hero; the diagram is a literal product sketch, not decoration; copy sits inside the diagram's whitespace.
landing-hero.color_rule: Dark-mode base (charcoal, not pure black), one accent glow hue tied to the brand, off-white edge lines for the diagram.
landing-hero.rendering_finish: Technical-drawing precision — thin line weights, dimension-like labels, soft bloom on active nodes, no heavy textures.
signature_moves: node + edge as primary composition language
one accent-hue glow on active nodes
copy flows through the diagram whitespace

landing-hero.name: Vercel monochrome poster hero
landing-hero.reference_work: vercel.com product pages and Vercel Ship keynote design
landing-hero.compositional_grammar: Type-led poster: massive display typography as the visual subject with a single geometric support element (triangle, arrow, monogram); no art — the type IS the art.
landing-hero.color_rule: Strict two-color: off-white + off-black, OR brand base + single accent; no third color allowed.
landing-hero.rendering_finish: Print-poster precision — tight letter-spacing, generous line leading, high contrast, offset-print texture minimal.
signature_moves: display type at 10x the scale of body copy
one geometric support mark, never more
poster-print tactility — visible but quiet grain
example_bans: three or more colors in the composition

landing-hero.name: Criterion Collection film-still hero
landing-hero.reference_work: Criterion Collection DVD/Blu-ray covers, Janus Films title cards
landing-hero.compositional_grammar: Letterboxed cinematic framing: the hero image is a single resonant film-still composition (whether photographic, illustrated, or 3D); title typography sits at the edge or bottom band with studied restraint.
landing-hero.color_rule: Film-stock palette (warm 1970s Kodachrome OR cool monochrome) with one bold type-hue; saturation disciplined below 70%.
landing-hero.rendering_finish: Archival-photography softness or hand-painted illustration — never sharp-digital; subtle grain; film-letterbox proportion.
signature_moves: 16:9 letterbox with intentional top/bottom negative bands
one resonant image holds the whole meaning
title-card typography near-edge, never centered-giant

landing-hero.name: Swiss graphic agency 1975
landing-hero.reference_work: Josef Müller-Brockmann posters, Otl Aicher's Lufthansa system, Grapus
landing-hero.compositional_grammar: Strict underlying 12-column grid visible as quiet rule, single-color accent placed with mathematical intention, headline typography dominates, no decorative elements — every mark is structural.
landing-hero.color_rule: Off-white or pale ground + one primary accent (red, blue, or yellow) + black typography; the accent is never background, always mark.
landing-hero.rendering_finish: Offset-print matte, crisp edges, disciplined negative space, no gradients, no noise.
signature_moves: grid visible as underlying structure
one primary-hue accent placed with intention
headline typography carries the voice, not imagery

campaign-poster.name: Pentagram poster-house print
campaign-poster.reference_work: Pentagram posters by Paula Scher, Domenic Lippa, Harry Pearce
campaign-poster.compositional_grammar: Typographic dominance: headline/declaration occupies 50-70% of the frame, supporting image or mark anchors a corner; modular print-grid discipline underneath; the poster reads loud at 10ft, readable at 1ft.
campaign-poster.color_rule: Two colors max, both saturated, deliberately chosen; the color pairing carries the poster's whole voice.
campaign-poster.rendering_finish: Offset-print tactility — visible print texture, quiet registration imperfection, confident saturation without neon.
signature_moves: typography at declarative scale (not timid)
two-color print discipline
supporting mark or photo anchors a single corner
example_bans: decorative illustration competing with the type

campaign-poster.name: Paul Rand IBM-era poster
campaign-poster.reference_work: Paul Rand's IBM eye-bee-M, Westinghouse, and UPS work
campaign-poster.compositional_grammar: One dominant playful symbol, plain single-tone background, minimal supporting mark — the poster communicates one idea with one symbol and nothing else.
campaign-poster.color_rule: Primary-color palette (red, blue, yellow) on pale or black ground; 2 colors max; confident without being neon.
campaign-poster.rendering_finish: Flat poster color with visible offset-print grain, crisp geometric edges.
signature_moves: one symbol holds the whole meaning
primary-color palette with confident restraint
negative space treated as intentional sculpt

campaign-poster.name: Saul Bass title-design poster
campaign-poster.reference_work: Saul Bass posters and title sequences (Anatomy of a Murder, Vertigo, The Man with the Golden Arm)
campaign-poster.compositional_grammar: Reductive iconography — the subject distilled to its most elemental silhouette or geometric gesture; typography as integral graphic element, often cut or torn-edge; the composition reads as a narrative moment, not a product shot.
campaign-poster.color_rule: Two or three colors, at least one bold and one restrained; off-white/off-black plus one hue carries most work.
campaign-poster.rendering_finish: Hand-cut collage texture — torn edges, visible paper grain, imperfect registration; not digital-sharp.
signature_moves: one silhouette as the whole subject
typography integrated with the silhouette, not laid over it
hand-cut paper-collage energy
example_bans: digital-sharp vector edges with no texture
more than 3 colors in the composition

campaign-poster.name: Neville Brody Face-magazine editorial
campaign-poster.reference_work: Neville Brody's The Face covers and early FUSE issues
campaign-poster.compositional_grammar: Layered typographic collage, custom-cut letterforms, graphic distortion and masked-off passages; the composition reads as sampled from a cultural moment, not designed for a brand deck.
campaign-poster.color_rule: Punchy editorial palette — saturated hues used in 2-3 bold blocks, black typography tension throughout.
campaign-poster.rendering_finish: Hand-cut and photocopied feel — visible paper, tape seams, distortion, intentional imperfection.
signature_moves: custom-cut or layered typography as primary subject
saturated color blocks carry mood
collage seams and distortion visible

campaign-poster.name: Swiss graphic declaration poster
campaign-poster.reference_work: Josef Müller-Brockmann music-festival posters, Jan Tschichold constructivist posters
campaign-poster.compositional_grammar: 12-column underlying grid, headline sized to break out of the grid with confident overflow, one geometric mark (circle, diagonal, bar) as visual anchor, rest is negative space.
campaign-poster.color_rule: Pale or black ground + one primary-hue accent (red/blue/yellow) + black typography; the accent is never decorative.
campaign-poster.rendering_finish: Offset-print matte; crisp geometric edges; disciplined whitespace; no gradients.
signature_moves: headline overflows the grid at massive scale
one geometric mark as compositional anchor
primary-hue accent used once, precisely
